text:
Zoe (Design): Quick copy help — new error card on eval runs that fail with model mismatch. Current card says: "Eval failed. See logs." Users in support keep asking what to do next. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal.mock/snap/eval-fail-card.png

Leah (Support): Short version: people want actionable next steps. They want to know if they should rerun, pick another model, or file a bug. Also they copy-paste the error code to tickets; include it visibly.

Arun (ENG): Backend returns error.kind = {model_mismatch, OOM, timeout, infra}. For model_mismatch we know suggested fallback models if available. We can show contextual CTAs: "Switch model" or "Rerun with same model". Also we log an error_code like ERR_EVAL_MM_7.

Samira (A11y): Microcopy rules: put the action verb up front. For screen readers avoid vague phrases like "See logs". Instead: "View logs" or "Open run details". Add sr-only prefix for error code: "Error code: ERR_EVAL_MM_7" and ensure the card uses role="alert" so assistive tech announces it.

Zoe (Design): Draft microcopy options:
- Option 1 (help-first): "Eval failed: model mismatch. Suggested action: try a compatible model or open logs." CTAs: [Switch model] [Open run details]
- Option 2 (direct): "Eval failed. This model is incompatible with the eval config. Choose a compatible model or adjust the config." CTAs: [View compatible models] [Edit eval]

Leah (Support): Prefer Option 2 but shorten. Support wants a one-line reason then two clear CTAs. Also include the error code under the line so support can copy it. Tone: calm, directive. No scary words like "fatal".

Arun (ENG): Implementation note: we can surface a small inline list of compatible models (up to 3) and a link to view all. If none, show Learn how to adjust the eval config. Also ensure CTAs are primary-first in DOM.

Samira (A11y): A11y specifics: 1) Card should have role="status" not alert if non-blocking, but for failed evals users expect immediate announcement so alert is OK. 2) Ensure focus is not stolen — clicking a CTA opens a new panel but focus should move predictably. 3) The error code should be visually hidden from clutter? No, show it visibly and also include sr-only explanatory text: "Copy error code to include in support request."

Zoe (Design): Revised copy candidate to add to the PR:
"Eval failed — model mismatch. This model is incompatible with the eval configuration. Suggested next steps: choose a compatible model or edit the eval settings.
Error code: ERR_EVAL_MM_7" CTAs: primary "View compatible models" secondary "Open run details" Link: "Learn how to update evals" (opens docs)

Arun (ENG): I'll wire up the model suggestions and include error_code in the UI payload. PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/6011 — includes copy variants and accessibility attributes. Preview: https://preview.redwood-internal/mock/eval-error/v1 (expires 48h) :gear:

Leah (Support): I'll update our canned responses to point to the new CTAs and include the exact phrasing so we can say: "Click View compatible models" when helping customers. Small ask: make the error code text selectable so we can copy quickly.

Samira (A11y): Quick nit: change CTA label from "Open run details" to "View run details" for verb consistency. Also ensure the docs link has descriptive link text: "How to update eval settings" rather than generic "docs".

Zoe (Design): Good catches. Final copy for PR: "Eval failed — model mismatch. This model is incompatible with the eval configuration. Suggested next steps: choose a compatible model or edit the eval settings.
Error code: ERR_EVAL_MM_7" CTAs: primary "View compatible models" secondary "View run details" Link: "How to update eval settings". I'll add the sr-only helper: "Copy the error code when contacting support."

Arun (ENG): Updated PR with Samira's accessibility tweaks and Leah's selectable error code. Tagging @Zoe for design sign-off.

ci-bot: preview deploy ready: https://preview.redwood-internal/mock/eval-error/v1 (expires 48h) :white_check_mark:

Zoe (Design): Looks good in preview. Merging after tests. Thanks everyone :sparkles:
